DROPPED, AND THE ARCHIVE HAS EARNED THE RIGHT TO. The tree makes Rocco Arena the son of Orazio Arena and Giovanna Zirilli. FIVE INDEPENDENT READS SAY OTHERWISE. His OWN BIRTH ACT, Scilla Nati 1861 atto 228, makes him the son of FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA and SERAFINA ARLOTTA. His OWN MARRIAGE ACT, Matrimoni 1888 atto 63, says «ARENA ROCCO... FIGLIO DI FRANCESCO ANTONIO... E DI SERAFINA ARLOTTA». Act 45 of 1860 gives that same couple a son GIUSEPPE -- and the tree gives Orazio exactly two children, Rocco and Giuseppe, so the tree has taken Francesco Antonio's household whole and hung it on Orazio. Meanwhile Orazio and Giovanna's REAL children are documented across four years -- Teresa 1853, Domenico 1856, Domenico 1859, Maria Annunziata 1860 -- and NONE of them is Rocco or Giuseppe. The 1856 and 1859 Tavole were read complete. The archive even tested the obvious namesake: act 60 of 1858 is another Rocco Arena, of Santo Arena and Giovanna Gioffre, and he is not this one either. ROCCO NOW HAS NO PARENTS ON THE CHART, because his real ones are not in Michael's export. That is the true state of the evidence and it is what work list row 51 exists to fix.

KEPT, AND FLAGGED, BECAUSE THE SURNAME IS WRONG AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT SETTLED. Act 206 of 1883 names his mother GIOVANNA ROMANO, and so does the New Orleans manifest of 1908 -- two independent records, two continents, one of them from his own mouth at twenty-four. The tree calls her GIOVANNA PONTILLO. THE EDGE IS KEPT because she is almost certainly the same woman under a wrong surname rather than a different person: same given name, same place, same household. WHAT IS NOT SAFE IS WHAT SITS ABOVE HER. If she is a ROMANO, then the GIUSEPPI PONTILLO and NUNZIATTA PONTILLO the tree gives her as parents are not this family's ancestors at all -- three more people on the spine resting on a surname the registers contradict. See the work list.

Pizzo, Morti 1829, atto 7, and the chancery's certified copy of it filed in the Briatico marriage bundle of 1849 as the groom's «avo paterno» -- the fede di morte of the paternal GRANDFATHER, which is what proves the descent rather than merely asserting it. Pasquale Prostamo, widower of Caterina, dead at Pizzo in January 1829.

KEPT, AND THE NAME IS IN DISPUTE. The export calls Pasquale Prostamo's wife CATERINA DI MEIO, born 1762. The Pizzo register of 1829 calls her CATERINA MAJO -- and this archive has already corrected its own reading of that name once, from «Muso» to «Majo», against both the original and the 1849 certified copy. Same woman, two surnames, and her own act has never been read.
